info.description:
The task board: projects, tasks with a per-project spoken
handle (ABC-12), the DRAFT→TODO→IN_PROGRESS→QA→UAT→DONE flow
plus CANCELLED, assignees and reporters by nick, dependencies,
subtasks, labels and components. Every status move and
assignee write is published to the board_events Redis stream.

The board also serves an MCP endpoint on /mcp, which is not
described here.
info.title: Task Board

get.description:
The labels that exist on the project's tasks — closed ones
included, which is why a label can answer with 0 — ordered by
the number of open tasks carrying them, busiest first. This is
the list a caller chooses from when tagging, and a label not
here is added by writing it on a task: there is no registry.
get.summary: List a project's labels with their open-task counts

post.description:
Registers a line of work with its own numbering. The key is
upper-cased and must be an uppercase letter followed by 1 to 9
more letters or digits; creating a project that already exists
is a 400.

400.description: invalid key or the project already exists

delete.description: Refused while the project still holds tasks; it does not cascade.

put.description:
Replaces the whole list — that is also how a
component is removed, and there is deliberately no additive
form: a registry you can only grow is a label. Blanks and
duplicates are normalised, the way a labels list is.
Refused with 409 and the number of such tasks while a value the
new list drops is still the component of one of the project's
tasks; clear it on them first (PATCH with "component": "").

409.description: a value the list removes is still held by the project's tasks

get.description:
Every item is the task without its long texts: description,
acceptance_criteria and summary_report are absent from the
answer, and GET /tasks/{id} is the one that answers them.
All filters are optional. status takes a comma-separated list
from the flow's vocabulary; ready=true and open=true are each
refused together with status (open=true and ready=true is
allowed — ready is already open); order is number, updated or
created (the default). label is repeated for more than one:
every named label must be on the task, so ?label=a&label=b ANDs.

parameters.description: Only tasks born here (the origin link, as stored)
parameters.name: origin

parameters.description: Only tasks assigned to this nick; none: only unassigned ones
parameters.name: assignee

parameters.description: A handle (ABC-45, any case) finds that task, a bare number that number in every project; anything else is a case-insensitive piece of the goal
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Only tasks carrying this label; repeat the parameter for tasks carrying all of them
parameters.name: label

parameters.description: Only tasks with this component — one of the project's components
parameters.name: component

parameters.description: true: only TODO tasks with no open dependency and no open subtask
parameters.name: ready

parameters.description: true: only tasks that are not DONE or CANCELLED
parameters.name: open

get.description:
The id segment takes the UUID or the spoken handle ABC-12;
they identify the same row.
get.summary: Get a task by UUID or spoken handle

parameters.description: Task UUID or a handle like ABC-12
parameters.name: id

400.description: neither a UUID nor a handle

delete.description:
Takes the task's thread with it. Refused, with 409 naming which,
while the task has children or while tasks were born in its thread.

409.description: still has children or tasks born in its thread

patch.description:
Edits goal, description and acceptance_criteria. A field that
was not sent cannot be cleared, and identity — project, handle,
origin, reporter — is not offered at all. discussion sets the
link to the chat the task is talked over in. labels, when
sent, replaces the whole set; [] clears them, and labels not
sent are left alone. component, when sent, must be in the
project's list (400 naming the list otherwise); "" clears it,
and not sending it leaves it alone.

put.description:
null hands the task back to nobody; "" is a 400 — omit the
field or send null to mean none. Every successful write is
published to the board_events stream.

parameters.description: assignee (a nick), or null to unassign
parameters.name: assignee

put.description:
Replaces the whole set; an empty list clears it. A link to an
unknown task, to the task itself, or into a longer cycle is a 400.

post.description:
The only way from IN_PROGRESS to TODO: the task also goes to
its reporter, and the reason becomes a line in its thread from
actor_id — all in one write. For an executor giving up and for
a watcher whose budget ran out. Published to board_events as
an ordinary move. A task anywhere but IN_PROGRESS is a 409.
post.summary: Put work in progress back in the queue

put.description:
The move must be legal from the task's current status; setting
the status it already has is a no-op 200. The vocabulary is
DRAFT, TODO, IN_PROGRESS, QA, UAT, DONE, CANCELLED; there is
no REVIEW and no BLOCKED. With from, the task must
also be in that status, or the answer is 409: this is how a task
is claimed, since two claimants sending from=TODO cannot both win.
A successful move is published to the board_events stream.
put.summary: Move a task through the flow

409.description: illegal transition from the current status, or the task is not in from

put.description: What was done, why, and where the artefacts are. Blank is refused.

get.description:
Answers if the process is serving HTTP at all, and says nothing
about Postgres. version is the git describe of the tree the
binary was built from, so a deployment can be compared with
its checkout to find services running stale code.

200 when a ping to Postgres succeeds, 503 when it does not.
This is what a compose healthcheck should ask, so a stopped
database turns the container unhealthy. Kept apart from
/health on purpose: /health must keep answering with the
version while the database is down, because a reader of the
version treats any non-200 as unreachable.
get.summary: Readiness probe: can this instance reach Postgres

503.description: status unavailable and the ping error

component.description:
Component is one of the project's components: absent means the
task has none, and a value outside the project's list is a 400 naming
the list. Unlike labels there is a registry, because it is the project's
property.

labels.description:
Labels are free-form tags; absent or empty is an ordinary
task, answered back as []. The service normalises them, so a caller
sending " bug ", "bug" and "" stores the single label "bug".

component.description:
Component, when sent, must be in the project's list or the patch is a
400 naming the list; sent as "" it clears the value, which is the only
endpoint for unsetting it — "not sent" must leave it alone.

discussion.description:
Discussion links the chat the task is talked over in, set by whoever
opens it.

components.description:
Components is the project's own list: a task's component is
one of these, and a list that removes a value a task still carries is
refused. Always non-nil — the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', so a
project without components answers [] and never null.

blocked_by.description:
BlockedBy is derived, never stored: the handles of the dependencies that
are not yet DONE or CANCELLED. This is the answer to the question a status
called OPEN or BLOCKED would have answered, and it cannot drift out of
agreement with the graph because there is nothing to keep in agreement.

Handles rather than ids because the only thing anyone does with this is
read it or say it — "ABC-15 is waiting on ABC-12".

blocks.description:
Blocks is the other edge of the same graph, derived on every read and
never stored: the handles of the tasks waiting on this one. It is the
second half of the question a card should answer — "ABC-2 is in UAT, and
because of it ABC-4 stands" — and it inherits BlockedBy's guarantee:
there is nothing stored, so there is nothing to drift out of agreement
with the links table.

The DONE or CANCELLED filter sits on this side, the reverse of where
BlockedBy puts it: a closed task holds nothing, so the subquery answers
empty for one. On the wrong side, a closed task would still claim to be
holding.

closed_at.description:
ClosedAt is when the task entered DONE or CANCELLED; null while open. A
trigger keeps it (migration 0004), whichever query moved the status.

component.description:
Component is the one value this task draws from the project's list: the
list is the project's, the choice is the task's. nil is "no component" —
a task spanning several components has none, and they can be recorded as
labels instead — which is why this is nullable
where Labels is not: an absent component is a state, an absent label set
is just no labels.

depends_on.description: DependsOn is what this task waits on, in the order the links were made.

labels.description:
Labels are free-form tags: a fixed vocabulary would decide in
advance what may be said about the work. Always non-nil — the column is
NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', and the service normalises what is written, so a
task with no labels answers [] and never null.

open_subtasks.description:
OpenSubtasks is derived the same way: the handles of this task's
children that are not yet DONE or CANCELLED. A task with any is not
ready (repository.go, List), and this is where a reader sees why.

origin.description:
Origin is where the task was born, Discussion where it is talked over:
links the board keeps and never opens, and either may be absent.

points.description:
Points is the estimate, like story points: nil is "not estimated", a
different fact from an estimate of 1.

summary_report.description:
SummaryReport is what was done, why, and where the artefacts are — shaped
like a commit message. Nullable because a task that has not been worked
has nothing to report, and an empty string would claim otherwise.
